question.leadin: During this war, UN forces were set back to a 140-mile defense line known as the "Pusan Perimeter" due to multiple defeats by the KPA.
question.text: Name this 1950s war that never ended with a peace treaty, but instead with the establishment of the DMZ. The U.S. and Soviet Union divided the namesake country of this war along the 38th parallel.
question.clue: Matthew Ridgeway replaced a general in this war who had turned the tide by landing an army behind enemy lines at Incheon.

swap.leadin: Operation Paul Bunyan involved the use of overwhelming military force to chop down a tree in this area.
swap.text: Name this area which separates North and South Korea from each other. The Joint Security Area within this zone is used for diplomatic meetings.

question.leadin: Answer the following about a certain class of warship.
question.text: An earlier example of an ironclad warship was this type of ship developed by Admiral Yi Sun-sin to resist a 16th century Japanese invasion of Korea. Named for the shape of the animal on its bow, these ships boasted cannons and a hull covered in spikes.
question.clue: Soldiers from Ming China helped defend Korea from Japanese invasion at the end of the 16th century. During that conflict, Korean Admiral Yi utilized these crazy awesome vessels which received their name from the appearance caused by their armored decks.

swap.leadin: Name these places identified with the Korean War.
swap.text: This village in the DMZ was the location of the peace talks between the two sides, and talks still go on just outside this village.
swap.clue: This village which hosted a more famous conference that led to the armistice between United Nations forces and communists in 1953 during the Korean War.

question.leadin: This landmass's Goreyo dynasty was overthrown by the Joseon.
question.text: Name this peninsula, whose Silla kingdom allied with the Chinese Tang to the northwest.
question.clue: A military commander employed by a kingdom in this region designed so-called "turtle ships" to counter the forces of Toyotomi Hideyoshi; that commander was Yi Sun-Sin.

swap.text: The Three Kingdoms period consisted of clashes between the Silla, Goguryeo (koh-KUR-yoh), and this Korean state in the southwest, which was governed from Hansong and was ruled by Geunchogo (gwen-CHOH-goh).
swap.clue: This kingdom absorbed all of the lands of the Mahan confederacy, thus seizing all of the present-day Jeolla ("jul-lah") region, under its great ruler Geunchogo ("geun-choh-goh").

question.text: This dynasty during the Three Kingdoms Period divided its people into "true bone" and "sacred bone," and it was founded by Hyeokgeose. The people of this dynasty later conquered the Goguryeo and Baekje empires.
question.clue: This dynasty employed a cultured class of cosmetic-using soldiers called the "flowering knights," or "hwarang."

swap.leadin: The first president of this nation was overthrown in the April Revolution because he rigged the election.
swap.text: Name this nation that disputes the possession of the Liancourt Rocks with an eastern neighbor.
swap.answerHtml: South Korea (accept Republic of Korea, prompt on Korea)
swap.clue: This country's first female leader led it from 2013 until her 2017 impeachment.

question.leadin: Answer these questions about a recurring theme in Asian history, kidnapping.
question.text: This South Korean's criticisms of Park Chung-hee's Yushin Constitution had him moments from being flung overboard in a pair of cement shoes before the kidnappers chickened out. This democratic activist later won the Nobel Peace Prize and served as president from 1998 to 2003.
question.clue: Pope John Paul II interceded to save this man from being executed after the Gwangju People's Uprising.

swap.leadin: Identify the following about the history of Buddhism in Korea.
swap.text: Warrior monks in the Righteous Army were active participants in the first of these events. After a brief exile, Admiral Yi Sun-shin led his forces to victory in the Battle of Myeongnyang (myung-n'YAHNG) during one of these events.
swap.answerHtml: Japanese invasions of Korea [or Toyotomi Hideyoshi's invasions of the Korean peninsula; or Imjin War; or Wanil Korean Campaign; or Bunroku no ek; or Keichō no eki; or Kara iri]
swap.clue: That one of these events eventually ended at the Battle of Noryang.

question.leadin: Regulations on this country's unofficial Jangmadang markets that keep men under 60 from participating have resulted in women being responsible for an estimated 70% of household incomes.
question.text: Name this Asian "Hermit Kingdom" whose Songun form of military-first resource allocation has been maintained under the long rule of its Kim family.
question.answerHtml: North Korea [or Democratic People’s Republic of Korea or DPRK or Choson-minjujuui-inmin-konghwaguk; reject “Republic of Korea”]
question.clue: One leader threatened this country with "fire and fury like the world has never seen."

swap.text: A period of this name in earlier Korean history involved states like Baekje ("pek-cheh") and Silla. Another period of this name in China included conflicts between Zhuge Liang ("JOO-guh LYONG") and Cao Cao ("tsao tsao").
swap.clue: The "Later" part of a period with this name was dominated by a Unified Silla that conquered Goguryeo.

question.text: Members of this Joseon noble, scholarly class were expected to be knowledgeable in the Confucian classics. To enter this class, one had to perform well on the gwageo civil service exam.
question.clue: This class which constituted the aristocracy of a kingdom which was the last to select its officialdom through the gwageo examination system.

swap.text: The Korean peninsula was introduced to Buddhism from China in the fourth century CE by Sundo, who mainly proselytized in this kingdom. Baekje, Silla, and this kingdom comprised the Korean Samhan.
swap.clue: Some of the best-preserved art of this kingdom survives in the tomb of Dong Shou at a complex at Anak.

question.leadin: This kingdom is traditionally said to have been founded by Hyokkose.
question.text: Name this kingdom that unified a peninsula after conquering neighboring Paekche and Koguryo with the help of the Tang Dynasty, then expelled Tang forces.
question.clue: This kingdom included the hereditary "head rank 6" caste in its "bone rank" system, and used highly-educated elite knights whose name means "flower boys."

swap.text: The only other Korean ruler to receive the epithet "The Great" was this man, a king of the Goguryeo. His son erected a twenty-three foot tall stele on his gravesite honoring his expansive victories.

question.leadin: Guerrillas in this uprising set up bases in the caves around Hallasan, an extinct volcano where remains of victims can still be found, and attacked paramilitary troops of the Northwest Youth League.
question.text: Name this massacre that lasted over a year from April 1948 to 1949, in a nation being occupied under Operation Blacklist Forty.

swap.text: Qing forces were supported by this Korean dynasty, which was founded by Yi Seonggye after the fall of the Goryeo and lasted until it was conquered by the Empire of Japan.
swap.clue: Admiral Yi Sun-sin successfully defended this kingdom from two Japanese invasions.

question.leadin: Now located at the National Library of France, it was composed by the Buddhist monk Baegun around 1372 AD, and published by his students Seoksan and Daldam. FTPE.
question.text: Name this two-volume Korean anthology of Zen Buddhist teachings which is the oldest existing metal-plate printed book.

swap.leadin: It began when Wang Kon united the kingdoms of Goguryeo, Silla and Baekje.
swap.text: Name this Korean dynasty that reigned from 918 to 1392.
swap.clue: Twenty-nine women from hojeok ("HO-juck") families were married to this dynasty's founder, Wang Geon ("gun").
